newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciller slams Turkey's exclusion from EU aspirants.
newsitem.headline: Ciller slams Turkey's exclusion from EU aspirants.

text.p: Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller on Tuesday bitterly criticised the exclusion of Turkey from a group of countries told by the European Union that they can aspire to full membership.

In a speech in Rome on the eve of talks with five key European colleagues, she said: "We do not want any special relationship (with the EU). Either Turkey is a full member or she will not hang in as a second-rate member."

Turkey sees the 15-nation EU's attitude as a hostage to Greek bias. Cyprus and Malta have been told they can expect EU accession talks to start, probably in 1998, and nine countries from eastern and central Europe are to be judged on suitability.

"Now it is celebration time for the new Europe. Now the 15 have designated 11 more for potential new members. Everyone is in except for one country -- only Turkey. Only Turkey is left out," Ciller said.

Listing reasons why Turkey should be eligible to join, she said that "if it does not occur, I feel it will be one of the largest mistakes of history because it will hurt the feelings of the Turkish people irreversibly and the choice will be made".

Ciller is due to meet in Rome on Wednesday with the foreign ministers of Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Spain for talks on Turkey's relations with Western Europe amid signs of growing strain. The meeting is not in the EU framework.
